newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe ex-president said to have raped policeman.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe ex-president said to have raped policeman.

text.p: Zimbabwe police on Tuesday announced an investigation into charges of homosexual rape against ex-president Canaan Banana, lifting the lid on a scandal brewing for months under the government of President Robert Mugabe.
Lawyers for a former aide who says he was abused by Banana during the five years he acted as his aide de camp said they intended to sue the former head of state for damages.
"We are going into investigations immediately," Zimbabwe Republic Police (ZRP) Commissioner Augustine Chihuri told the official ZIANA news agency.
"These are allegations that have been made and before (the investigations) I cannot say much more than that," he added.

The aide, Zimbabwean police inspector Jefta Dube, was convicted on Monday of murdering a fellow policeman who goaded him by calling him "Banana's wife". He says he was forced into a subservient homosexual relationship by his onetime boss.

"We will definitely be filing for damages...and we are now working out the details," Dube's lawyer, Byron Hove, told Reuters. He called Banana's alleged behaviour "gross, callous and cruel abuse of his official position".

Dube was sentenced to 10 years in jail on Monday for the 1995 fatal shooting of his fellow officer. He told the court his homosexual subjugation by Banana had made him depressive and alcoholic, and the judge ruled that Dube's case should be treated as one of diminished responsibility.

The allegations were likely to embarass President Mugabe, who has taken a hardline stance against homosexuality. Over the last two years Mugabe has described gays as perverts "who are worse than dogs and pigs" and said those who paraded as gays must be lynched.

Banana, who retired from his largely ceremonial presidential post in December 1987 after seven years in office, was not called to answer Dube's allegations, but Justice David Bartlett ordered police to investigate the case further.
The judge also lifted a ban on reporting Dube's charges, imposed when the case went to court late last year.
Dube told the court that Banana first abused him in June 1986 after inviting him for dinner at his Harare State House.

"After dinner, he invited me to dance to some ballroom music in his office and study. I said I could not dance but he said he would teach me. During the dance I realised his penis was getting erect, and he was drawing much closer. He gave me a long, deep French kiss before I excused myself and disappeared," he said.

Dube alleged that Banana finally raped him in December 1986 in one of the state guest rooms. He said he later tried to resist Banana's advances but the then-president responded by ordering his arrest, accusing him of insubordination and threatening him with dismissal.
"After that I accepted his advances, out of fear and because I realised nothing was going to happen to him because of his position," Dube said.
Dube said he reported the sexual abuse to his police bosses, and a report had been made to then-Vice Prime Minister Simon Muzenda who ordered his transfer in late 1987.

Former Assistant Police Commissioner John Chademana who handled Dube's homosexual complaint, said the police were aware of "numerous intelligence reports" that Banana, who is married with four children, was involved in homosexual affairs.
